title: Console onboarding nudges — copy + trigger rules (v1)
body:
Context / goal
- Goal: lift Activation (first successful, production-like inference call) and early retention (repeat usage in week 1–2) for self-serve devs.
- This doc is the working copy deck + rules for Console onboarding nudges shipped behind feature flag + experiment assignment.
- Primary definition of “activated” for v1 measurement: first_request_success (first 2xx completion for a chat/text generation request) within 72h of signup. Secondary milestones: api_key_created, first_streaming_success, dashboard_viewed (latency/cost).

Audience
- New self-serve signups (primary)
- Returning signups who have not reached activation
- Lapsed users returning to Console (secondary, low pressure)

Nudge surfaces in scope (v1)
1) Activation checklist module (persistent, dismissible)
2) Banner A: “1 step away” (after key created but no success)
3) Banner B: “Troubleshoot errors” (after repeated request errors)

Global copy principles (developer-first)
- Be concrete: name the exact action (Create API key, Run curl, Enable streaming).
- Use neutral tone; avoid guilt / nagging.
- Avoid over-promising (“fastest”, “best”, “guaranteed”). Prefer measurable terms (“see latency + token cost breakdown”).
- Default to verbs + code-oriented CTAs (“Copy curl”, “Open Quickstart”).
- Keep banners skimmable: 1 headline, 1 sentence, 1 primary CTA, optional secondary.
- Don’t block usage; nudges should never be modal for v1.

Experiment + variants (naming)
- Experiment name (assignment key): console_onboarding_nudges_v1
- Randomization unit: user_id (sticky)
- Variants:
  - control: no checklist, no banners
  - treatment_a: checklist + banners (copy set A)
  - treatment_b: checklist + banners (copy set B; lighter tone)
- Holdout: 5% (always no nudges) for guardrail comparison.

Instrumentation requirements (events)
For each surface, emit view + click + dismiss:
- nudge_viewed
- nudge_clicked
- nudge_dismissed
Required properties:
- nudge_id (string; see IDs below)
- nudge_variant (control/treatment_a/treatment_b)
- placement (dashboard_home, project_overview, api_keys_page, quickstart_page)
- project_id
- step_id (for checklist)
- cta_id
- locale (e.g., en-US)
- is_returning_user (boolean)

Related activation funnel events (from taxonomy)
- signup_completed
- api_key_created
- first_request_attempted (optional if available)
- first_request_success
- first_streaming_success
- dashboard_viewed (with dashboard_name = latency_cost)
- billing_added

Nudge IDs (stable string keys)
- checklist.activation_v1
- banner.one_step_away_v1
- banner.troubleshoot_after_errors_v1
- banner.streaming_tip_v1 (optional if we ship; see backlog)

----------------------------------------
1) Activation checklist module
----------------------------------------
Placement
- Default location: Console dashboard home (top of page; below global nav, above metrics)
- Secondary placement: Project overview page (if user navigates there first)

Show rules
- Show if user has NOT fired first_request_success for any project.
- If user has fired first_request_success: hide permanently.
- If user dismisses checklist: hide for 7 days OR until next session after 7 days; do not re-show more than 3 times total.
- If user has multiple projects: checklist is user-level, but step CTAs should route to the “current project” context.

Checklist header copy
- Title (A): “Get to your first successful inference call”
- Title (B): “Ship your first call in minutes”
- Subtitle (A): “Complete these steps to verify your setup and see latency + token costs.”
- Subtitle (B): “Verify your API key, run a request, then check latency + cost.”

Checklist steps (step_id, completion event, copy, CTA)
Step 1
- step_id: create_api_key
- Completion: api_key_created
- Label (A): “Create an API key”
- Label (B): “Create your API key”
- Helper (A): “Keys are scoped to your org and used for requests.”
- Helper (B): “You’ll use this key in curl/SDK calls.”
- Primary CTA: “Create key” -> /settings/api-keys (or in-context drawer)
- Secondary link (optional): “API keys docs” -> docs link

Step 2
- step_id: run_first_request
- Completion: first_request_success
- Label (A): “Run your first request (2xx)”
- Label (B): “Make a successful request”
- Helper (A): “Use curl or the SDK. We’ll mark this complete after a successful response.”
- Helper (B): “A 2xx response completes activation tracking.”
- Primary CTA (contextual):
  - If SDK detected (utm/sdk or docs referrer): “Open SDK quickstart” -> /docs/quickstart?tab=sdk
  - Else: “Copy curl example” -> opens code snippet drawer

Step 3
- step_id: enable_streaming
- Completion: first_streaming_success
- Label (A): “Try streaming responses”
- Label (B): “Enable streaming”
- Helper (A): “Lower time-to-first-token and improve UX for chat.”
- Helper (B): “Stream tokens to render faster.”
- Primary CTA: “View streaming example” -> /docs/streaming

Step 4
- step_id: view_latency_cost
- Completion: dashboard_viewed (dashboard_name=latency_cost)
- Label (A): “View latency + token cost breakdown”
- Label (B): “Check latency and cost”
- Helper (A): “See p50/p95 latency, tokens, and estimated spend per route/model.”
- Helper (B): “Track tokens and latency per model.”
- Primary CTA: “Open dashboard” -> /console/observability/latency-cost

Step 5 (optional / “next step”)
- step_id: add_billing
- Completion: billing_added
- Label (A): “Add billing (recommended)”
- Label (B): “Add billing to remove limits”
- Helper (A): “Avoid interruptions as you scale usage beyond free credits.”
- Helper (B): “Unlock higher quotas when you’re ready.”
- Primary CTA: “Add billing” -> /settings/billing
- Notes: this step should be clearly marked “Optional” for early onboarding; avoid pressure.

Step 6 (optional)
- step_id: invite_teammate
- Completion: teammate_invited (if exists) else track via nudge_clicked only
- Label (A): “Invite a teammate”
- Label (B): “Bring your team in”
- Helper (A): “Share API keys, routes, and dashboards across your org.”
- Helper (B): “Collaborate in the Console.”
- Primary CTA: “Invite” -> /settings/members

Empty / completed states
- If Step 1 complete but Step 2 incomplete: visually emphasize Step 2.
- If Steps 1–2 complete but Step 3 incomplete: do not display “warning”; just “Next recommended”.
- If all steps complete (including optional): replace module with a compact success card for 7 days:
  - Title: “You’re live.”
  - Body: “Next: create a route, set a fallback policy, or explore Dedicated/Private options.”
  - CTA: “Create a route” -> /console/routes/new

Accessibility notes for copy
- Avoid emoji-only meaning.
- CTAs must be descriptive out of context (“Open latency + cost dashboard” vs “Open”).

----------------------------------------
2) Banner A — “One step away”
----------------------------------------
Intent
- Catch users who created an API key but haven’t gotten a successful request.

Placement
- Project overview page and dashboard home.

Show rules
- Show when:
  - api_key_created = true
  - first_request_success = false
  - AND user has been signed up >= 10 minutes (avoid showing instantly)
- Hide when:
  - first_request_success fires
  - OR user dismisses banner (hide for 14 days)
- Frequency cap: max 1 view per day.

Copy options
Variant A
- Headline: “You’re one request away from activation.”
- Body: “Run a quick curl/SDK call to verify your setup. We’ll mark activation after a successful 2xx response.”
- Primary CTA: “Copy curl example”
- Secondary link: “Troubleshooting”

Variant B
- Headline: “Ready to test your API key?”
- Body: “Make a successful request to confirm everything’s wired up.”
- Primary CTA: “Open quickstart”
- Secondary link: “See common errors”

CTA routing
- Primary CTA should deep-link into the quickest path based on context:
  - If user has no project selected: route to create/select project first.
  - If on project page: open inline snippet with project + model prefilled.

Tracking
- nudge_id: banner.one_step_away_v1
- cta_id: copy_curl | open_quickstart | open_troubleshooting

----------------------------------------
3) Banner B — “Troubleshoot after repeated errors”
----------------------------------------
Intent
- Reduce drop-off after auth/config errors during first request attempts.

Placement
- Dashboard home and request logs page (if they land there).

Show rules
- Show when (rolling 10-minute window):
  - request_error_count >= 2
  - AND first_request_success = false
  - AND error_class in {auth, permissions, invalid_request, rate_limit, network}
- Hide when:
  - first_request_success fires
  - OR user dismisses (hide for 30 days)
- Frequency cap: max 2 views per day.

Error-class specific headline/body (dynamic)
If error_class = auth (e.g., 401)
- Headline: “Auth error: check your API key.”
- Body: “Make sure the key is active and sent in the Authorization header. If you rotated keys, update your env vars.”
- Primary CTA: “Open API keys”
- Secondary link: “Auth troubleshooting”

If error_class = permissions (e.g., 403)
- Headline: “Permission error: your key may be scoped incorrectly.”
- Body: “Verify org/project access and key permissions. Support can help if you’re unsure.”
- Primary CTA: “Review key permissions”
- Secondary link: “Contact support”

If error_class = invalid_request (e.g., 400)
- Headline: “Request error: validate model + parameters.”
- Body: “Double-check the model name and required fields. Use the quickstart snippet to compare.”
- Primary CTA: “Open request example”
- Secondary link: “API reference”

If error_class = rate_limit (e.g., 429)
- Headline: “Rate limited: try a smaller test call.”
- Body: “You may be hitting a limit during setup. Start with a short prompt, then scale up.”
- Primary CTA: “View limits”
- Secondary link: “Add billing”

If error_class = network/timeouts
- Headline: “Having trouble connecting?”
- Body: “Check outbound network rules and retry. Streaming can also help reduce perceived latency.”
- Primary CTA: “Retry with streaming example”
- Secondary link: “Status page”

Tracking
- nudge_id: banner.troubleshoot_after_errors_v1
- Properties should include:
  - error_class (string)
  - last_error_code (string/int)
  - request_sdk (if known)

Support guardrails
- If “Contact support” is present, track clicks as guardrail signal (support-link clicks) to monitor unintended confusion.

----------------------------------------
Localization / i18n considerations
----------------------------------------
Locales
- v1 shipping only: en-US
- Prepare strings for future: de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP (per broader console i18n roadmap)

String construction rules
- Use full sentences; avoid idioms (“one step away” may not translate cleanly).
- Keep placeholders explicit and reusable:
  - {projectName}
  - {modelName}
  - {sdkName}
  - {docsUrl}
- Avoid embedding punctuation around placeholders that varies by language.

Length constraints (practical)
- Banner headline target: <= 48 characters in English.
- Banner body target: <= 120 characters in English (will expand in German; allow wrapping).
- CTA button target: <= 20 characters in English.

Terminology glossary (must be consistent)
- “API key” (not “token”)
- “Streaming” (not “server-sent events” in UI copy)
- “Latency” + “token cost” (avoid “price per token” in UI; pricing page is canonical)
- “Activation” should be internal-only; in UI copy prefer “first successful request” unless headline variant explicitly uses activation.

Claims / compliance
- Do not mention benchmark numbers in Console nudges (keep those in marketing pages where substantiation links are maintained).
- Avoid “SLA”, “guaranteed uptime” language in self-serve UI.

Notes for ja-JP (future)
- Prefer short, direct verbs; avoid heavy loanwords where a standard product term exists.
- “Streaming” likely kept as ストリーミング, but confirm with localization vendor.

Notes for de-DE (future)
- Expect 20–35% expansion; ensure buttons can expand.

----------------------------------------
Open questions / TODO
----------------------------------------
- Do we want to use the word “activation” in Variant A banner headline, or keep it developer-visible but neutral? (Product/PMM to confirm.)
- For error banner: can we reliably classify error_class server-side vs client-side? If not, default to generic troubleshooting copy.
- Step 5 “Add billing”: confirm whether we show only after a threshold (e.g., >X tokens attempted) to avoid early friction.
- Confirm exact Console routes for API keys, billing, dashboards (SUP-2841 indicated some routing churn).

Approval checklist
- PM (Marissa Cole): triggers + placements
- Growth (Ben Carter): experiment variants + success criteria alignment
- Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson): UTM attribution consistency (if any links go to landing pages)
- Analytics (Paula Mendes / Logan Wright): event names + required properties
- Support (Dev Patel): troubleshooting language + escalation link

Revision history
- 2025-01-10: Initial draft created (Kenji)
- 2025-01-14: Added error-class dynamic copy + frequency caps (Kenji/Tessa)
- 2025-01-18: Updated checklist steps to match activation definition (Marissa/Paula)
- 2025-01-22: Added i18n guidance + compliance notes (Soojin review pending)
